critic_changes: Population thread: the World Bank Economic Update quote was wrong. The page reads "as population growth absorbed almost the entire arithmetic gain from a declining rate", not "...from the country's upper-middle-income status". I replaced it with the page's words and changed the text to match what it supports: the number of poor barely fell from 2017 to 2024.

Arc, sentence 4: I removed "offset gains in wood, manganese and public works". The 2026 sources say wood and manganese shrank or underperformed in 2025, and none of them describes gains in those sectors. The sentence now names the shocks and what they hit (reserves and public debt), which the IMF passage supports. I also reworded "-0.6 over 2016-2025" to say income per person shrank 0.6 percent a year, which matches G1 avg_10y.

Arc, sentence 2: I changed "debt and political unrest slowed reforms". The 2013 World Bank report says foreign debt and arrears built up and that unrest weakened the adjustment programs. It does not say debt slowed reforms.

Arc, sentence 5: I changed "led by public building while oil, mining and timber underperformed" to the MPO's own terms: large infrastructure projects, with oil, manganese and wood exports underperforming. I also tied the sentence to 2025.
Headline: I replaced "kept growth near zero", which is wrong for the 1999-2009 era at -3.1, with "held growth back".

Oil fields thread: the text says reserves shrank and exploration was limited, but the cited quote only supports the 1997 peak. I added a second IMF passage that names maturing fields, dwindling reserves and limited exploration.

Oil price shocks thread: the old IMF quote listed the crises but did not support "hit reserves and public debt". I swapped it for a 22-word passage from the same page that names the impact on reserves and public debt. I also removed 2008-2009 from the thread text because the new quote no longer covers it.
Adjustment thread: no quote backed "deep cuts to public building". I added the 2013 World Bank passage on large cuts to capital spending and changed the wording to "public investment".
Spending thread: I removed "2023-2025 political transition" because the sources give no dates for it, and replaced "state-led building push" with the MPO's "surge in public investment".

since_last_year: I added citations for the claims that had none: the MPO passage on the oil-backed loan and Eurobond, and the World Bank Economic Update passage on 2025 oil output. I also changed "unpaid bills" to "arrears", the word the MPO uses.

Tension: I kept it because the 2013 report does call 2003-2010 a recovery with GDP per capita rising. I replaced the 2024/2025 point. The World Bank's own 2025 per-capita estimate is higher than the data file's 0.3, so the real disagreement is between the two figures, not about output versus per-capita growth. I quoted no number that is absent from the data file.

growth_story.headline: Gabon's income per person is still 55.2 percent below its 1976 oil-boom peak, as aging oil fields and repeated oil price shocks held growth back.
growth_story.arc: Gabon's income per person peaked in 1976, at the height of an oil boom, and is still 55.2 percent below that peak, about where it first was in 1972. From 1990 to 1998 it grew 1.1 percent a year as oil output rose toward its 1997 peak, while foreign debt and arrears built up and political unrest weakened reform programs. From 1999 to 2009 it shrank 3.1 percent a year, as oil production fell from that peak with the fields aging, and the 2008-2009 crisis hit an economy tied to oil. Since 2010 it has grown only 0.4 percent a year, and it shrank 0.6 percent a year over 2016-2025, as the 2014-2016 commodity slump, the 2020 pandemic and falling oil output hit reserves and public debt. The World Bank describes growth in 2025 as led by large infrastructure projects, while oil, manganese and wood exports underperformed.

threads.title: Oil fields past their peak
threads.text: Gabon's oil output peaked in 1997 and has drifted down since, as fields aged, reserves shrank and exploration was limited. Oil output fell again in 2025.

threads.text: Swings in the oil price have repeatedly knocked income back. The 1986 price collapse ended the boom years, and later collapses, including in the 2014-2016 commodity slump and the 2020 pandemic, hit reserves and public debt hard.

threads.text: After the 1986 crash Gabon went through several adjustment programs with deep cuts to public investment. From 1990 the move to multiparty politics brought unrest that weakened those programs.

threads.title: Spending with the oil cycle
threads.text: Public spending has tended to rise and fall with oil prices, so little oil wealth was saved and debt was high by 2023. After the political transition, a surge in public investment widened the budget deficit sharply in 2025.

threads.title: A fast-growing population
threads.text: The population is growing quickly, so total output growth turns into much smaller gains in income per person. The World Bank finds the number of poor people barely fell between 2017 and 2024, as population growth absorbed almost all of the fall in the poverty rate.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank's 2013 growth report calls 2003-2010 a recovery in which income per person rose steadily, helped by high commodity prices and reforms, but the data file shows income per person falling in most of those years, inside a 1999-2009 era that averaged -3.1 percent a year. For 2025 the World Bank's 2026 update also reports income per person rising faster than the 0.3 percent in the data file.
